blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: To interact with an object, we need to anticipate both how it will move and how our hands should move with it. Human videos capture these relationships across everyday activities, offering a natural source for learning to predict future interactions. Learning from them requires recovering motion from completed interactions and using it to anticipate what could happen next. We present $\textit{Grasping-the-Future}$, a unified generative model of joint 3D hand-object motion, including wrist motion, finger articulation, and object position and orientation. Through masked spatiotemporal completion and flow matching, we train a single model for several prediction tasks: forecasting future interactions, predicting hand motion given object motion or vice versa, generating both trajectories toward a desired final object pose, and completing partially observed interactions. We explicitly model hand-object relations and incorporate contact constraints to help preserve grasp relationships during motion. To obtain 3D supervision from internet videos, we develop a scalable pipeline that combines pretrained perception models with joint geometric optimization to reconstruct completed interactions. We combine these recovered trajectories with annotated interaction datasets as training data for all tasks. We demonstrate strong performance across all tasks, outperforming released forecasters on datasets with 3D annotations. Moreover, we show geometric and physical plausibility of the predicted trajectories by retargeting them to a robotic embodiment. Videos are available at https://grasping-the-future.github.io.
blocks.zh: 为了与一个物体互动,我们需要预见它将如何移动,以及我们的双手应如何与之一起移动。 人类的视频捕捉到日常活动中的这些关系,为学习预测未来互动提供了自然来源. 从中学习需要从已完成的相互作用中恢复运动,并利用它来预测接下来会发生什么。 我们呈现$\textit{Grasping-the-Future}$,一个统一的三维手-物体联合运动的基因模型,包括手腕运动,手指发音,以及物体位置和取向. 通过遮掩的瞬态完成和流相匹配,我们为几个预测任务训练出一个单一的模型:预测未来的相互作用,预测给定物体运动的手动,反之亦然,生成两个向所期望最终物体姿势的轨迹,完成部分被观测到的相互作用. 我们明确模拟手物关系,并纳入接触限制,以帮助在运动中保持抓住关系。 为了从互联网视频中获取3D监督,我们开发了可伸缩的管道,将预先训练的感知模型与联合几何优化结合起来,以重建已完成的相互作用. 我们把这些恢复的轨迹与附加说明的相互作用数据集结合起来,作为所有任务的训练数据. 我们在所有任务中展现出强效的性能,在3D注释的数据集上表现优于发布的预报器. 此外,我们通过将预测的轨迹重新瞄准机器人的外观来显示几何和物理上的合理性。 视频可在https://grasping-the-future.github.io上查阅。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: “Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.” — Søren Kierkegaard
blocks.zh: “生活只能向后理解;但必须向前理解。” - 瑟伦·基尔凯加尔德

blocks.en: To interact with an object, we need to anticipate how our actions will affect it. Placing a mug on a shelf is a simple everyday action, but predicting how it will unfold requires understanding how the hand and mug move together. The fingers must hold the mug as it is lifted and release it only once it rests on the shelf. The way the mug is grasped affects how it can be carried, and the position of the shelf affects where the hand needs to move. From the eyes of the human manipulating, parts of the hand or the object may be occluded, and several plausible future motions may be possible. Anticipating the interaction therefore requires predicting the motion of both the hand and the object, while preserving firm hand-object contact as the object moves through the 3D world.
blocks.zh: 为了与一个物体互动,我们需要预见我们的行动将如何影响它。 把一个杯子放在架子上是一种简单的日常动作,但预测它会如何展开,需要了解手和杯子是如何一起移动的. 手指必须握着杯子 当它被抬起来时 并释放它 只有在它躺在架子上。 抓住杯子的方式会影响如何携带,架子的位置会影响手需要移动的地方. 从人类操纵者的眼中,手或物体的部位可能会被吞噬,未来可能还会有几种可能的运动. 因此,预测相互作用需要预测手和物体的动向,同时在物体穿过3D世界时保持牢固的手物体接触.

blocks.en: Human videos are a natural source for learning these predictions, showing how people handle objects across many everyday situations. Learning from them involves two steps: first, extracting hand and object motion from completed interactions, and then using these examples to learn how an interaction might continue from a partial observation. These steps echo Kierkegaard’s distinction: a recorded video allows us to look back and understand what happened, while acting requires anticipating what comes next. Image-based predictions, such as generated videos, can leave relative depth and contact ambiguous. Predicting in 3D makes the spatial relationships between the hands, objects, and scene explicit: where the fingers touch the mug, how it is oriented as it is carried, and where it comes to rest on the shelf. This geometric description also provides an unambiguous reference for later retargeting the predicted motion to a different embodiment like a robot.
blocks.zh: 人类视频是学习这些预测的自然来源,显示人们如何在日常生活中处理物体。 从中学习涉及两个步骤:第一,从已完成的相互作用中提取手和物体运动,然后用这些例子来学习从局部观察中如何继续一种相互作用. 这些步骤与Kierkegaard的区别相呼应:录制的视频让我们可以回顾和理解所发生的事情, 基于图像的预测,如生成的视频,可能留下相对的深度和接触模糊. 3D中的预测使得手,物体,和场景之间的空间关系变得明确:手指触碰杯子的地方,背着杯子时如何定向,在架子上休息的地方. 这种几何描述也为后来将预测的运动重定向到一个像机器人这样的不同的化身提供了明确的参考.

blocks.en: Our key insight is that a single model can learn these different forms of prediction: predicting an object’s trajectory given the hand’s motion, predicting the hand’s trajectory given the object’s motion, generating both trajectories given a desired final object pose, and forecasting or completing an interaction from partial 3D observations. People reason this way intuitively: watching a hand move suggests where an object will go, while imagining where an object should end up suggests how the hand needs to move. We present Grasping-the-Future , a unified generative model of joint 3D hand-object motion. The same model forecasts an interaction from a short observed context, predicts hand trajectories given object motion or object trajectories given hand motion, generates motion toward a desired object pose, and fills gaps between observed poses (Figure 1 ). Across these tasks, we must handle observations of different entities and times. We bring these tasks together through masked spatiotemporal completion: we reveal different parts of a hand-object trajectory to the prediction model, and a flow-matching objective learns to generate the missing pieces of the trajectory. The generated trajectories include wrist motion, finger articulation, and object position and orientation. Since plausible hand and object trajectories can still drift apart, we use explicit hand-object relations and contact constraints to keep them moving together during a grasp.
blocks.zh: 我们的关键洞察力是,一个单一的模型可以学习这些不同的预测形式:根据手的运动来预测物体的轨迹,根据物体的运动来预测物体的轨迹,根据理想的最终物体的姿势来产生两种轨迹,以及从部分三维观测中预测或完成一种相互作用。 人们直觉地解释了这个原因:看手动会暗示一个物体会去的地方,而想象一个物体最终会去的地方会暗示手需要如何移动. 我们提出Grasping-the-Future, 一个统一的基因模型 联合3D手动物体。 同一模型预测了从短期观测到的上下文的相互作用,预测了给定物体运动的手轨或给定物体运动的手轨,产生向理想物体姿势的运动,并填补了观测到的姿势之间的空隙(图1). 在这些任务中,我们必须处理不同实体和时间的观察。 我们通过遮盖的瞬间完成来把这些任务结合起来:我们向预测模型揭示一个手物体轨迹的不同部分,一个流比目标学习生成轨迹缺失的片段. 生成的轨迹包括手腕运动,手指发音,以及物体位置和方向. 由于可能的手和物体的轨迹仍然可以飘移,所以我们使用明确的手-物体关系和接触限制来保持它们在抓住时的移动.

blocks.en: Learning this predictive model requires 3D hand-object supervision that large-scale internet videos do not directly provide. We therefore develop a scalable pipeline that combines pretrained perception models with joint geometric optimization to extract hand-object trajectories from complete monocular videos. The pipeline separates camera motion from object motion, refines the alignment between the hands and object using contact and temporal constraints, and filters unreliable reconstructions. We extract over 62,000 62{,}000 trajectories from internet videos and combine them with existing annotated hand-object datasets in a common 3D representation, accounting for differences in annotation quality during training. On egocentric video, our reconstructions are on par with or slightly better than those of HOPformer ( Bansal et al., 2026 ) , a recent model for egocentric images. From third-person viewpoints, our hand error is about nine times lower and our object pose error about a quarter lower (Appendix B.3 ). The reconstructed trajectories serve as pseudo-ground truth for all tasks.
blocks.zh: 学习这个预测模型需要3D手物监督,大规模互联网视频并不直接提供. 因此,我们开发了一个可伸缩的管道,将预先训练的感知模型与联合几何优化相结合,从完整的单视视频中提取手物体轨迹. 管道将相机运动和物体运动区分开来,利用接触和时间限制来细化手和物体的对接,并过滤不可靠的重建. 我们从网络视频中提取超过62 000 62{,}000个轨迹, 并将其与现有的注解手标数据集结合, 与HOPFOR(Bansal等人, 2026年)相比, 从第三人称视角来看,我们的手误差大约低9倍,我们的对象构成的误差大约低四分之一(附录B.3 ). 重建后的轨迹成为所有任务的伪地真理.

blocks.en: We evaluate Grasping-the-Future across forecasting and conditional generation tasks on datasets with 3D annotations, including OakInk2 ( Zhan et al., 2024 ) and HOT3D ( Banerjee et al., 2025 ) , and on held-out internet videos using our extracted trajectories as pseudo-ground truth. On the annotated datasets, a single forecast from Grasping-the-Future has 17 % 17\% lower final wrist error and 10 % 10\% lower final object error than the best released methods. The same model also predicts object motion from hand motion, which none of these methods supports, with 63 % 63\% lower final error than keeping the object rigidly attached to the hand. We also demonstrate that these predictions can guide robot manipulation: by retargeting the predicted human motion to simulated robot hands with SPIDER ( Pan et al., 2026 ) , we enable the hands to manipulate objects along the forecast trajectories for different types of manipulation tasks.
blocks.zh: 包括OakInk2(Zhan等人, 2024年)和HOT3D(Banerjee等人, 2025年), 以及使用我们提取的轨迹作为伪地真相的互联网视频。 在附加说明的数据集上,来自Grasping-the-Future的单一预测中,最终手腕误差为17% 17\%,最终对象误差为10% 10\% 10\% 较最佳发布方法更低. 同一种模型还预测物体运动来自手动,这些方法都没有支持这种运动,比保持物体刚性附着在手上还要低63%的终极错误. 我们还表明,这些预测可以指导机器人的操纵:通过将预测的人类运动重新瞄准模拟机器人手与天基信息平台(Pan et al., 2026年),我们使双手能够操纵各种类型的操纵任务的预测轨迹上的物体.

blocks.en: In summary, our contributions are threefold. We develop a unified generative model of 3D hand-object motion that supports forecasting, cross-entity prediction, goal-conditioned generation, and temporal completion through a common masking formulation. We propose a scalable pipeline for reconstructing temporally aligned hand-object trajectories from internet videos and using them as supervision for learning future interactions. We incorporate explicit hand-object relations and geometric contact constraints into trajectory generation, producing structured 3D predictions that we evaluate through robot retargeting and object manipulation.
blocks.zh: 总之,我们的贡献有三重。 我们开发了一个统一的三维手物体运动基因模型,通过常用的遮盖配方支持预测,跨实体预测,目标有条件生成,以及时间完成. 我们提出一个可扩展的管道,用于重建互联网视频中暂时一致的手表轨迹,并将其作为学习未来互动的监督。 我们把明确的手物体关系和几何接触限制纳入轨迹生成,产生结构化的3D预测,我们通过机器人重定向和物体操纵来评估.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Reconstructing hand-object interactions from video. Recent methods recover 3D hand-object geometry and motion from monocular videos by combining visual observations with geometric and learned priors ( Hasson et al., 2021 ) . Joint priors over hand configurations and object shape support reconstruction and grasp synthesis ( Ye et al., 2024 ) , while temporal attention helps recover coherent hand trajectories ( Ye et al., 2026a ) . Other methods reconstruct bimanual interactions using Gaussian splatting ( On et al., 2025 ) or use novel-view synthesis priors to recover object geometry that is not visible in short clips ( Wang et al., 2025b ) . Hand priors also support joint hand-object pose estimation from a single egocentric image ( Bansal et al., 2026 ) . Recent work recovers world-space hand and object motion from egocentric videos with known object templates and supports hand-guided interaction synthesis ( Ye et al., 2026b ) . We build on these advances to extract supervision from completed human interactions. Our focus is on using the recovered trajectories to learn how an interaction unfolds over time from a partial observation.
blocks.zh: 从视频中重建手物体交互. 近代方法通过将视觉观测与几何学和所学前科相结合,从单视视频中恢复3D手物体几何和运动(Hasson等人,2021年). 手部配置和物体形状的联合前身支持重建和抓取合成(Ye等人,2024年),而时间关注则有助于恢复一致的手部轨迹(Ye等人,2026a). 其他方法使用高斯电镀(On et al., 2025)重建双人交互(On et al., 2025)或使用小说视角合成前缀来恢复短片中看不到的物体几何(Wang et al., 2025b). Bansal等人,2026年。 最近的工作是用已知的物体模板从以自我为中心的视频中恢复世界空间手和物体运动,并支持手制导的交互合成(Ye等人,2026b ). 我们利用这些进展,从已完成的人类互动中获取监督。 我们的重点是利用恢复的轨迹,从局部观测中了解相互作用如何随时间演变。

blocks.en: Interaction forecasting and robot manipulation. Prior work predicts hand trajectories and interaction hotspots from egocentric video ( Liu et al., 2022 ) . Recent methods account for uncertainty in future 3D hand motion ( Bao et al., 2023 ) , use language queries to guide trajectory prediction ( Bao et al., 2025 ) , and combine interaction reasoning with 3D hand motion prediction ( Chen et al., 2026b ) . Forecasting object poses ( Soraki et al., 2026 ) and 3D point trajectories ( Bharadhwaj and Jangir, 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ) further describes how objects move during an interaction. Some methods model the relationship between human and object motion by conditioning object forecasts on hand motion ( Thakkar et al., 2025 ) or combining diffusion with physics-informed correction for full-body human-object forecasting ( Xu et al., 2023 ) . Other work forecasts motion in unconstrained videos through dense 2D point trajectories ( Thakkar et al., 2026 ) . These predictions can also guide robot manipulation. HOPMan translates predicted human interaction plans into robot actions ( Bharadhwaj et al., 2024a ) , while Track2Act combines predicted point tracks with geometric transfer and a residual policy ( Bharadhwaj et al., 2024b ) . Gen2Act learns policies conditioned on generated human videos ( Bharadhwaj et al., 2025 ) . We learn to predict articulated hand motion together with object pose, capturing how the fingers, wrist, and object move through an interaction. We then retarget these forecasts to simulated robot hands to test their use for manipulation.
blocks.zh: 互动预测和机器人操纵. 先前的作品预测手轨和互动热点来自以自我为中心的视频(Liu等人,2022年). 最近的方法说明了未来3D手动的不确定性(Bao等人,2023年),使用语言查询来指导轨迹预测(Bao等人,2025年),并将交互推理与3D手动预测(Chen等人,2026年b)相结合. 预测物体的姿势(Soraki等人,2026年)和3D点轨迹(Bharadhwaj and Jangir,2026年;Zhang等人,2026年)进一步描述了物体在相互作用过程中的移动情况. 一些方法模拟人与物体运动之间的关系,方法是在手动时调节物体预测(Thakkar等人,2025年),或结合扩散与物理学知情的校正来进行全身人体物体预测(徐等人,2023年). 其他工作通过密集的2D点轨迹在不受约束的视频中预测运动(Thakkar等人,2026年). 这些预测也可以指导机器人操纵. HOPMan将预测的人类互动计划转化为机器人行动(Bharadhwaj et al., 2024a),而Track2 行为将预测的点轨与几何转移和残余政策相结合(Bharadhwaj等人,2024b) 。 。 。 Gen2Act学习以生成的人类视频为条件的政策(Bharadhwaj等人,2025年)。 我们学会了预测清晰的手动与物体的姿势, 捕捉手指,手腕和物体如何通过相互作用。 然后我们重新锁定这些预测 模拟机器人的手 测试它们用于操纵

blocks.en: Controllable motion synthesis. A complementary line of work, often motivated by graphics and animation, generates plausible motion from text, object geometry, reference grasps, or goal poses. These methods typically emphasize generation plausibility without necessarily requiring grounding the predictions in a real scene. Prior work synthesizes dynamic grasps from a grasp reference and a desired object pose using physics-based control ( Christen et al., 2022 ) . Bimanual manipulation datasets also provide models for completing task primitives ( Zhan et al., 2024 ) . Text-conditioned methods generate hand-object motion through contact-guided diffusion ( Cha et al., 2024 ) or masked latent flow matching ( Chen et al., 2026c ) , while other work separates global motion from local hand articulation using latent diffusion and a grasp VAE ( Li et al., 2025a ) . Some methods ground generated motion through initial human-object poses and sparse object waypoints ( Li et al., 2024 ) . Masks over frames and joints also support sparse or partial motion constraints ( Cohan et al., 2024 ) . We ground our predictions in partial observations of a hand-object interaction and the surrounding scene geometry. In Grasping-the-Future , one model forecasts its continuation, predicts either entity from the other’s motion, generates both trajectories toward a desired object pose, and completes missing portions of an interaction while modeling hand-object contact.
blocks.zh: 可控运动合成. 往往以图形和动画为动机的辅助系列工作,从文字、物体几何、参考抓取或目标上产生可信的运动。 这些方法通常强调生成的可信度,而不一定要求将预测建立在真实的场景中。 先前的工作综合了动态的把握,从一个抓住的参照物和想要的物体的姿势中利用基于物理学的控制(Christen等人,2022年)。 双人操纵数据集也为完成任务原始数据提供了模型(Zhan等人,2024年). 文字条件方法通过接触导散射(Cha等人,2024年)或蒙面潜流比对(Chen等人,2026年c年)生成手物体运动,而其他工作则利用潜在散射和抓取VAE(Li等人,2025年a年)将全球运动与局部手表达分开。 一些方法的地面通过最初的人体物体的姿势和稀疏的物体中途点产生运动(Li等人,2024年). 遮罩过框和关节也支持稀疏或局部的运动约束(Cohan等人,2024年). 我们用部分观测数据来预测手物体的相互作用 和周围的场景几何 在Grasping-the-Future中,一个模型预测了它的延续性,从另一个模型的运动中预测出两个实体,生成两个向想要的物体摆姿势的轨迹,并在模拟手物体接触时完成一个相互作用缺失的部分.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: Figure 2: Model overview. An interaction is represented as a grid of tokens, with rows indicating states 𝐬 \mathbf{s} and relations 𝐫 \mathbf{r} , and one column per frame. Observed cells are given, and unobserved cells are initialized to noise. A transformer attends to rows, columns and across the grid to predict the flow velocity of the noise cells (with the context tokens (blue) as additional keys/values). The noise is decoded into a sample by ten Euler steps, producing hand and object trajectories. Multiple samples for the same input vs. ground truth (dashed). The bottom row is used for training. An observation mask is sampled per window during training so the same model trains on all tasks (but with a different set of observed cells). Flow matching is used for velocity supervision and auxiliary losses are applied to decoded trajectories.
blocks.zh: 图2:模式概述。 交互表示为符号网格,行表示状态为 s\ mathbf{s} 和关系为 r\ mathbf{r},每帧显示一列. 观察细胞被赋予,未观察细胞被初始化为噪声. 变压器会前往行,列和横跨网格以预测噪声细胞的流速(以上下文符号(蓝色)作为附加键/值). 噪声由十个欧拉步骤解码成样本,产生手和物体轨迹. 同一输入物的多个样本对地面真理(dashed). 下行用于训练. 在训练期间每个窗口都取样一个观察面具,所以在所有任务上都使用相同的模型列车(但有不同的一组观察细胞). 流量匹配用于速度监督,辅助损失应用于解码轨迹.

blocks.en: We develop Grasping-the-Future to predict how hands and objects interact with each other in 3D. We represent an interaction as a trajectory of hand and object poses. We observe a part of this trajectory, and our goal is to generate the rest. By changing which parts we observe, we use the same model to forecast the future, to generate the hand trajectory from a given object trajectory and vice versa, to generate the motion that reaches a given final pose, and to fill a gap in the middle of a trajectory. We first describe this representation and the prediction model and then introduce the losses that help maintain hand-object contact. Finally, we describe how we obtain 3D hand-object reconstructions from internet videos to create a dataset for training the model.
blocks.zh: 我们开发了Grasping-the-Future来预测手和物体在3D中如何相互作用. 我们作为手和物体的轨迹代表一种相互作用。 我们观察了这一轨迹的一部分,我们的目标是产生其余部分。 通过改变我们观测到的哪些部分,我们使用同样的模型来预测未来,从给定物体的轨迹产生手轨,反之亦然,产生达到给定最终姿势的运动,并填补轨迹中间的一个空白. 我们首先描述了这种表示和预测模型,然后引入有助于保持手物接触的损失. 最后,我们描述我们如何从互联网视频中获取三维手物重建,以创建用于培训模型的数据集。

blocks.en: 3.1 Problem Formulation
blocks.zh: 3.1 问题的提出

blocks.en: Representation. We segment each recorded interaction into windows of T T consecutive frames. A window contains up to two hands and one rigid object, which are the three entities we model. At frame k k , each hand e ∈ { L , R } e\in\{L,R\} has a state 𝐬 k e ∈ ℝ 99 \mathbf{s}^{e}_{k}\in\mathbb{R}^{99} made of the wrist position and rotation and the 15 15 joint rotations of the MANO hand model ( Romero et al., 2017 ) . The states of a window form 𝐗 \mathbf{X} . We also give the model a static context 𝐜 \mathbf{c} with the object mesh and its scale, the MANO shape of each hand, the gravity direction when available, and a point cloud of the scene.

blocks.en: Architecture and sampling. Each hand, object, or relation token is embedded into the feature space using a layer for its type. Both hands share a layer, as do both relation tokens, so a learned embedding identifies each of the five tokens. We also add a learned embedding for whether the token is observed or masked, a sinusoidal encoding of elapsed time, and a learned projection of its confidence. The confidence distinguishes annotated data from trajectories extracted from video (Section 3.4 ), so the model can rely less on noisy labels. The transformer repeats a group of four blocks. The first three attend to the five tokens over time and to each of the five tokens for each frame. The fourth attends over all tokens of all frames at once. Every attention layer also reads the context 𝐜 \mathbf{c} as extra key-value tokens, with the object mesh encoded by Uni3D ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) and the scene point cloud, carrying DINOv3 features ( Siméoni et al., 2025 ) , by LitePT ( Yue et al., 2026 ) . At inference, the masked tokens start as Gaussian noise and are denoised by integrating the predicted velocity over 10 10 Euler steps.

blocks.en: Existing annotated 3D datasets cover a limited range of objects, environments, and interactions, so we also extract hand and object trajectories from monocular internet videos and train on both (Section 4.1 ). Figure 3 summarizes the pipeline; we provide implementation details in Appendix B and compare the extracted trajectories with HOPformer on EPIC-Contact, HOT3D, and DexYCB in Appendix B.3 .
blocks.zh: 现有的附加说明的3D数据集涵盖有限的对象,环境和相互作用,因此我们也从单光的互联网视频中提取手和物体的轨迹,并同时对两者进行培训(第4.1节)。 图3总结了管道;我们在附录B中提供了实施细节,并在附录B.3中将提取的轨道与EPIC-接触、HOT3D和DexYCB上的HOPFormer进行比较。

blocks.en: Per-frame estimates. We use Molmo 2 ( Clark et al., 2026 ) to identify manipulation clips from Action100M ( Chen et al., 2026a ) and locate the manipulated object, then track its mask with SAM 3 ( Carion et al., 2025 ) . We estimate MANO hand poses with WiLoR ( Potamias et al., 2025 ) , object meshes and poses with SAM 3D ( Chen et al., 2025 ) , metric depth with MoGe ( Wang et al., 2025a ) , and camera motion with MegaSaM ( Li et al., 2025b ) .
blocks.zh: 每个框架的估计数。 我们使用Molmo 2(Clark等人,2026年)来识别来自Action100M的操纵剪辑. (Chen等人,2026a)并定位被操纵物体,然后用SAM 3(Carion等人,2025年)追踪其面具. 我们估计MANO手姿与WiLOR(Potamias等人,2025年),手姿与SAM 3D(Chen等人,2025年),手姿与MoGe(Wang等人,2025年a),手姿与MegASAM相机运动. (Li等人,2025b).

blocks.en: Trajectory refinement. Each per-frame estimate is in its own frame’s camera coordinates, so we use the MegaSaM camera poses to bring them into one world coordinate system. We lift CoTracker3 ( Karaev et al., 2025 ) object tracks into 3D with depth and fit a rigid object trajectory by robust bundle adjustment ( Huber, 1964 ) . We then jointly refine hand and object poses to match the 2D masks and keep contact, penalizing interpenetration, abrupt motion, and implausible finger poses, with hand scale fixed. When a held object is hidden for a long stretch, its rotation follows the hand’s. A transformer trained on corrupted motion-capture trajectories estimates each clip’s depth bias, which we correct by shifting the object and the grasping hand along the viewing direction. Finally, we smooth the remaining hand jitter (Appendix B.2 ).
blocks.zh: 轨迹完善. 每个帧的估算值都在它自己的相机坐标中, 所以我们用MegaSAM相机的姿势把它们带入一个世界坐标系统。 我们把CoTracker3(Karaev等人,2025年)物体轨迹提升到3D深处,并通过强力捆绑调整来适应刚性物体轨迹(Huber,1964年)。 然后我们联合改进手和物体的姿势,以匹配2D口罩并保持接触,惩罚穿透、突然移动和不可信的手指姿势,并固定手势。 当一个被持有的物体被长期隐藏时,它的旋转会跟随手. 一台训练有素的变速器 以腐蚀的动作捕捉轨迹来估计每个弹夹的深度偏差, 我们通过将物体和抓手沿视向移动来校正。 最后,我们平滑剩下的手触动(附录B.2 ).

blocks.en: Verification. Finally, we check image agreement, contact, interpenetration, temporal consistency, and object size. To make sure we tracked the correct object, we also ask a VLM to point to the object in the hand through the clip. Of the total candidate clips, about 12 % 12\% yield valid trajectories after final verification. For each verified trajectory, we also compute an interaction-fidelity score. A higher score means the reconstructed hand(s)-object contact fits the video better, the object motion is smoother, and the hands and object align better with their 2D detections. This score goes into the model as part of the confidence input. If a supporting surface is visible, we also estimate the direction of gravity from it.
blocks.zh: 核查。 最后,我们检查图像协议,接触,互穿,时间一致性,以及对象大小. 为了确保我们追踪到正确的物体,我们也要求一个VLM通过剪辑指向手中的对象. 在全部候选剪辑中,约12%的12\%在最终核实后产生有效轨迹. 对于每个经核实的轨迹,我们也计算出一个相互作用-忠诚的得分. 更高的分数意味着重建的手-对象接触更适合视频,物体运动更平滑,手和物体更符合他们的2D探测. 这个分数作为信心输入的一部分进入模型. 如果一个支撑表面可见,我们也估计其引力方向.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: Our experiments evaluate prediction across seven tasks and its transfer to robotic motion. We compare against non-learned baselines and released forecasting models from prior work, and evaluate the benefit of training on trajectories extracted from internet videos (Section 4.2 ). We then evaluate how well forecast trajectories transfer to robots (Section 4.3 ). Additional ablations on the model’s losses and inputs are provided in Appendix D .
blocks.zh: 我们的实验评估了7项任务的预测 以及它转移到机器人运动上的预测 我们比较了先前工作中未获得的基线和已发布的预测模型,并评价从互联网视频中提取的轨迹培训的益处(第4.2节)。 然后,我们评价对机器人转移轨道的预测如何良好(第4.3节)。 关于模型损失和投入的进一步情况见附录D。

blocks.zh: 4.1 设置

blocks.en: Training. We train on eight annotated hand-object datasets ( Chao et al., 2021 ; Banerjee et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2024 ; Zhan et al., 2024 ; Rim et al., 2026 ; Hampali et al., 2020 ; Kwon et al., 2021 ; Wang et al., 2024 ) and trajectories extracted from internet videos. Together, they provide 74,312 74{,}312 trajectories and 134,661 134{,}661 five-second windows, including 62,562 62{,}562 trajectories and 109,346 109{,}346 windows from internet videos. Each training window receives a task observation pattern sampled uniformly across the five task families, or a random block mask. Training details are provided in Appendix A .

We evaluate every task on the same 331 331 five-second windows from diverse scenarios unseen during training, 256 256 from the annotated datasets and 75 75 from internet videos, with one window per video. For forecasting, the model observes the first 0.5 0.5 seconds and predicts the remaining 4.5 4.5 seconds. For internet videos, the references are our extracted trajectories, which are less accurate than the annotations (Appendix C ). We will release the code and data publicly.

blocks.en: Metrics. We compare each prediction with the recorded trajectory of its window, which we call the reference, and measure position error in millimeters at the wrists and the object center. For a predicted trajectory, the average displacement error (ADE) is this error averaged over its generated frames, while the final displacement error (FDE) is the error at its last frame. When the final pose is observed, the final error is zero by definition, so we report the mid-gap error, calculated at the midpoint of the generated frames. Since a single observation can lead to multiple plausible futures, we generate 20 20 samples per input and evaluate the results in three different ways.. • Single sample. We score the first of the 20 20 samples on its own, as when the model is asked to make a single prediction. • Energy score. The energy score ( Gneiting and Raftery, 2007 ; Shahroudi et al., 2024 ) of the 20 20 samples is their average error minus half their average distance from each other. The second term rewards spread, while the first penalizes samples far from the reference. If we view the reference as one draw from all the futures that could follow the observation, the expected score is lowest when the samples come from the same distribution as those futures. A method that makes only one prediction has no spread, so its score equals its error and can be compared directly. • Best of 𝟐𝟎 \mathbf{20} . The error of the sample with the lowest ADE shows how close the nearest of the 20 20 samples comes to the reference. This sample is selected using the ground-truth reference, which is unavailable to the model at inference time. The energy score rewards both accuracy and spread, so we also check the spread on its own. Let x 1 , … , x 20 x_{1},\dots,x_{20} be the sample positions and x 21 = y x_{21}=y the reference position at the frame scored by FDE or mid-gap error, and let d i d_{i} be the distance from x i x_{i} to the mean of the other 20 20 positions. The reference lies inside the samples if d 21 d_{21} is not the largest of d 1 , … , d 21 d_{1},\dots,d_{21} . If the samples and the reference come from the same distribution, each d i d_{i} is equally likely to be the largest, so the reference lies inside the samples in 20 / 21 ≈ 95 % 20/21\approx 95\% of windows. A rate below 95 % 95\% means that the samples are too concentrated or centered away from the reference, and a rate above 95 % 95\% means that they are too dispersed. For all of these metrics, each annotated dataset counts equally, and annotated data and internet videos each count for half. Appendix C gives full definitions, eligibility rules, and additional interaction metrics.

We also compare with the prior released models for hand and object trajectory forecasting in Table 2 . Each released model uses its required inputs, and all predictions are evaluated with our scoring code.

blocks.en: 4.2 Prediction Across Tasks
blocks.zh: 4.2 跨任务预测

blocks.en: Table 1 compares our model with non-learned baselines across all seven tasks. When predicting one entity from the other’s motion, a single sample has 46 % 46\% lower object FDE and 37 % 37\% lower hand FDE than rigid carry. A single sample is less accurate than stay-put for forecasting ( 2 2 – 8 % 8\% higher error) and than interpolation at the middle of gaps whose endpoints are both given ( 3 3 – 28 % 28\% ). These baselines stay close to the observed poses, which is a safe guess when the future is uncertain. A sample instead commits to one plausible motion, and when this motion differs from the reference, its error can exceed that of not moving at all. The energy score accounts for this by scoring the 20 20 samples together, and under it our model scores 30 30 – 68 % 68\% lower than the best baseline in every task column. Since the energy score subtracts the distance between samples and a single prediction has none, part of this difference could come from spread alone. To test this, we give stay-put and interpolation the spread of our samples, turning each of their predictions into 20 20 samples with Gaussian noise that has the covariance of our samples in that window. With about the same spread, our score is still 9 9 – 44 % 44\% lower (Appendix E.1 ), so our samples also lie closer to the reference. Figure 4 shows examples across five tasks.

blocks.en: We also train the same model without the trajectories extracted from internet videos (“Motion capture only” in Table 1 ) to see how much they help. Compared with this model, a single sample of our model has 8 % 8\% lower forecasting FDE for objects and 15 % 15\% for hands, and 18 18 – 26 % 26\% lower FDE when predicting one entity from the other’s motion. When only the final pose of the hands or of the object is given, the FDE of the other entity is 14 14 – 23 % 23\% lower. On internet videos, the forecasting gain comes from motion across the image, where extracted references are more accurate than in depth (Appendix C ). Across the image, the final error falls from 112 112 to 73 73 mm for objects and from 155 155 to 83 83 mm for hands, while the error in depth barely changes. The reference also lies inside our samples more often, in 76 76 – 88 % 88\% of windows in every column (ideally 95 % 95\% ), against 46 46 – 75 % 75\% for the motion-capture-only model, whose samples are too close together.

blocks.en: Table 2 compares our model with released forecasting methods. Under the energy score, our ADE and FDE are 16 16 – 37 % 37\% lower than those of the best released method, ForeHand4D for the wrists and ObjectForesight for the object. When each method is scored on one prediction, our wrist ADE and FDE are 13 13 – 16 % 16\% lower than those of USST, the most accurate released method in this setting. For the object, MotionForesight has 11 % 11\% lower ADE and 5 % 5\% lower FDE than our single sample, but it barely moves the object. Its median predicted displacement at the end of the window is 18 18 mm, against 81 81 mm for the reference, and its FDE is within 1 1 mm of stay-put. The reference lies inside our samples more often than inside those of ObjectForesight, General Flow, and Uni-Hand ( 77 77 – 78 % 78\% versus 0 0 – 69 % 69\% ). ForeHand4D and MolmoMotion contain it more often ( 82 % 82\% and 95 % 95\% versus 76 % 76\% and 71 % 71\% ), but their samples are much farther apart and farther from the reference. They are on average 19 19 and 48 48 cm apart with errors of 22 22 and 42 42 cm, against 13 13 and 11 11 cm apart with errors of 16 16 and 15 15 cm for ours (Table 12 ). A set this wide contains the reference easily but provides poor motion predictions, which the energy score penalizes.

blocks.en: 4.3 Testing Physical Plausibility of Forecasting through Retargeting
blocks.zh: 4.3 通过重新瞄准来测试预测的物理可能性

blocks.en: We assess the physical plausibility of our forecasts by retargeting them to simulated XHands. We test whether the robot hands can manipulate the object and reproduce its predicted motion under the simulator’s dynamics.
blocks.zh: 我们通过重新瞄准XHands模拟来评估我们预测的物理可信度. 我们测试机器人手能否操纵物体,在模拟器的动态下复制其预测的运动.

blocks.en: Kinematic retargeting matches the robot’s wrist and fingertips to the predicted hand poses. Dynamic retargeting with SPIDER ( Pan et al., 2026 ) further optimizes robot controls in simulation to follow the predicted object motion. We also test kinematic retargeting with SPIDER’s grasp preparation but without trajectory optimization. Using only the observed frames, grasp preparation adjusts the robot hand’s starting pose and grip in simulation until the hand holds the object steadily. While the forecast hand holds the object, it then moves the robot wrist together with the predicted object and keeps the grip unchanged. All three methods use the same forecast for each observation.
blocks.zh: Kinematic 重定向将机器人的手腕和指尖匹配到预测的手姿势. 动态重定向与天基信息平台(Pan等人,2026年)进一步优化模拟中的机器人控制,以跟随预测的对象运动. 我们还试验以动态方式重新瞄准天基信息平台的掌握准备,但没有优化轨道。 仅使用观测到的帧,抓取准备会调整机器人手在模拟中的开始姿势和握力,直到手稳住物体. 在预测手握物体的同时,它随即将机器人手腕与预测的物体一起移动,并保持握力不变. 所有三种方法对每一项观测都使用相同的预测.

blocks.en: We evaluate 103 103 examples whose reference hand-object trajectories retarget successfully with SPIDER, and we run SPIDER with three optimizer seeds per example. We consider a retarget to be successful if the robot hand moves the object through the whole prediction interval and the object’s position and rotation errors relative to the forecast, averaged over the predicted frames, are below 100 100 mm and 0.5 0.5 rad.
blocks.zh: 我们评估了103个实例,其中参考手动物体轨迹与天基信息平台重新成功瞄准,我们以三个最佳种子管理天基信息平台。 我们认为,如果机器人手通过整个预测间隔移动物体,而相对于预测框架的预测,物体的位置和旋转误差低于100毫米和0.5弧度,则重新确定目标是成功的。

blocks.en: We see that kinematic retargeting succeeds in only 14.6 % 14.6\% of examples, showing that these manipulations are difficult to carry out under physics by matching wrist and fingertip poses alone (Figure 5 ). Grasp preparation raises success to 43.7 % 43.7\% , so many of these failures come from a grasp that does not hold the object. When the robot controls are also optimized with SPIDER, 73.8 % 73.8\% of our forecasts are reproduced in simulation. Once adapted to the robot hand, most of our forecast hand-object motions can therefore be carried out through physical interaction, which indicates that they are physically plausible.
blocks.zh: 我们只看到14.6%的14.6 %的例子成功地实现了动能重定向,这表明这些操纵在物理学下很难单独通过匹配手腕和指尖来进行(图5)。 格拉斯普准备将成功率提升到43.7% 43.7% \%,因此许多这些失败来自于一个不持有对象的把握. 当机器人控制也与天基信息平台进行优化时,73.8%的预测在模拟中重复。 因此,一旦适应机器人的手,我们大多数预测的手-物体运动都可以通过物理交互来进行,这说明这些动作在物理上是可信的.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We presented Grasping-the-Future , a unified model for forecasting and completing joint 3D hand-object motion. We combined masked spatiotemporal completion with explicit hand-object relations and contact supervision to predict coordinated motion under different observations and goals. We reconstructed over 62,000 62{,}000 trajectories from internet videos and showed that this supervision improved forecasting beyond training on annotated datasets alone. Under the energy score, our forecasts outperformed all released hand and object forecasting methods by 16 16 – 37 % 37\% . We also demonstrated that our forecasts could guide object manipulation after retargeting to simulated robot hands, connecting prediction from human videos to robot execution.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了Grasping-the-Future, 一个统一的模型 预测和完成联合3D手动物体。 我们把遮掩的瞬间完成与明确的手物关系和接触监督结合起来,预测在不同观察和目标下的协调运动。 我们重建了超过62 000 62{}000条网络视频轨迹, 在能量分数下,我们的预测比所有释放的手和物体预测方法都要好16 16 — — 37 % 37 — — — 。 我们还证明,我们的预测可以引导在重新瞄准模拟机器人手后进行物体操纵,将从人类视频到机器人执行的预测联系起来.

blocks.en: In this section we provide additional details on the model, losses and training from Sections 3.2 , 3.3 , and 4.1 . Also, Tables 4 and 5 provide information on the settings and loss weights.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们提供了第3.2、3.3和4.1节关于模式、损失和培训的更多细节。 此外,表4和表5提供了关于设置和减重的信息。

blocks.en: Representation. We divide each trajectory into five-second windows with a 2.5 2.5 -second stride, with the last window ending at the trajectory’s endpoint. Frames keep their timestamps and cover 5 seconds for each window, regardless of frame rate. So, a window can hold at most 150 150 frames for 30 30 fps recordings or about 50 50 frames for 10 10 fps extracted videos. We pad shorter windows (and windows from trajectories less than 5 seconds) and exclude padding and absent entities from attention and losses.
blocks.zh: 代表性。 我们把每个轨迹分成5秒的窗口, 2.5 - 2.5秒的步程, 最后的窗口结束于轨迹的终点。 帧保持时间戳,并覆盖每个窗口的5秒,无论帧速率如何. 因此,一个窗口最多可以持有150个帧,用于30个30个fps录音,或者大约50个帧,用于10个fps提取的视频. 我们设置更短的窗口(以及轨迹不到5秒的窗口), 并且将铺设和缺失的实体排除在注意力和损失之外。

blocks.en: The coordinates are as described in Section 3.1 , with two additional details. If the gravity direction is known, we also rotate them so that this direction points downward. When the object is unobserved at the present frame, centering uses the mean wrist position alone, and when no hand is observed there, the object alone.
blocks.zh: 坐标如第3.1节所述,另有两个细节。 如果重力方向已知,我们也会旋转它们,这样这个方向就会向下指向. 当物体在目前帧中未观测到时,中心点单独使用平均手腕位置,当那里没有观测到手时,单独使用物体.

blocks.en: Δ \Delta -codec. We compute rotation changes by subtracting consecutive 6-D rotation vectors, including those for finger joints. Relation tokens skip this encoding and describe each frame directly. The absolute observed states of Section 3.2 are standardized and paired with a flag, 1 1 when the state is observed and 0 0 otherwise. Both are zero at unobserved frames. They are mapped to a vector added to the state embedding by a linear layer initialized to zero, so they have no effect at the start of training.
blocks.zh: \Delta - 代码。 我们计算旋转变化的方法是减去连续的6-D旋转矢量,包括指关节的矢量. 关系符号跳过此编码并直接描述每个帧. 第3.2节的绝对观测状态是标准化的,与国旗配对,在观测状态时为1,另外为0。 两者在无人观察的框架中均为0。 它们被映射成一个向量,被一个线性层初始化为零嵌入到状态,因此在训练开始时没有效果.

blocks.en: Flow-matching loss. The flow-matching loss ℒ FM \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{FM}} is split into six components, for hand translation, wrist rotation, finger articulation, object translation, object rotation, and hand-object relations. Each component is the squared velocity error averaged over its channels and masked frames. Hand and relation components are computed for each side and averaged over the sides with masked frames. The weights in Table 5 combine the components into a weighted mean for each window, and the loss averages these means across windows. A component with no masked frames in a window is left out of that window’s mean, and a window with no masked frames is left out entirely. This averaging prevents over-weighting windows with many masked frames and components with many channels. For losses on decoded trajectories, we estimate clean tokens as 𝐱 ^ 1 = 𝐱 t + ( 1 − t ) ​ v θ \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{1}=\mathbf{x}_{t}+(1-t)v_{\theta} and decode them into poses.

blocks.en: Architecture. We use a 12 12 -block transformer with 512 512 -dimensional embeddings and eight attention heads, with the attention pattern and token embeddings of Section 3.2 . Each token type has a two-layer MLP that embeds it and a linear layer that predicts its flow velocity. Both hands use the same layers, and so do both relation tokens. AdaLN-Zero ( Peebles and Xie, 2023 ) gives every attention and feed-forward layer the flow time and the average time between frames. Another MLP takes the three state tokens and predicts fingertip contact, defined as a fingertip-to-object distance below 5 5 mm, and is trained with binary cross-entropy. Other settings are given in Table 4 .
blocks.zh: 建筑学. 我们使用12个12块的变压器,其中512个512维的嵌入式和8个注意头,其中的注意力模式和符号嵌入式为3.2节. 每个符号类型都有一个嵌入它的双层MLP和一个预测其流速的线性层. 两只手都使用同一层,两只关系符也一样. AdaLN-Zero(Peebles and Xie, 2023)对流线时间和帧之间平均流线时间给予了充分的注意和向导层. 另一个MLP取下三个状态符,并预测指尖接触,定义为指尖到5毫米以下的物体距离,并经过二进制交叉的训练. 其他设置见表4。

blocks.en: Each entity’s confidence features describe motion smoothness, stability of fingertip-to-object distances, presence in adjacent frames, and source quality. The relation token receives the confidence features of both its hand and the object. Smoothness and fingertip-distance stability are computed from neighboring frames, so close to a masked frame they can reveal the hidden pose. We therefore set them to 0.5 0.5 within 0.1 0.1 seconds of the entity’s masked frames. Fingertip distances depend on both the hand and the object, so for this feature we use the masked frames of both.
blocks.zh: 每个实体的自信特征都描述了运动的光滑性,指尖对物体距离的稳定性,相邻框架的存在,以及源的质量. 关系符号得到其手和对象的自信特征. 平滑度和指尖-距离稳定性是从相邻的帧中计算出来的,因此接近一个蒙面帧可以揭示隐藏的姿势. 因此,我们规定,在实体蒙面框0.1秒内,它们为0.5。 指尖的距离取决于手和物体,所以对于这个特性,我们使用两者的蒙面框.

blocks.en: Conditioning. The scene point cloud is derived from the final frame in which all entities are observed. This is because using partially observed frames might reveal a masked entity’s pose. We then remove the hand and object pixels using their masks. We then prune background points farther than 0.5 0.5 m from the hand-object midpoint, widening this to 1 1 or 2 2 m when too few points remain. We then downsample the point cloud to 4,096 4{,}096 points with farthest-point sampling and express it in the present frame’s centered coordinates.
blocks.zh: 条件 场景点云来源于观测所有实体的最终框架. 这是因为使用部分观测到的帧可能会揭示一个蒙面实体的姿势. 然后用面具去掉手和物体像素. 然后,在距离手目标中点0.5米远的地方,我们便把底点扩大至1、1或2米,因为剩下的点太少。 然后,我们把点云取样到4,096 4{,}096点,用最远的点取样,并用目前框架的中心坐标来表示。

blocks.en: Each scene point has 12 12 channels to pack the point’s position, surface normal, distances to the hands and object, height above the support plane, normal tilt from vertical, curvature, and log density. It also has 32 32 channels of PCA-reduced DINOv3 image features ( Siméoni et al., 2025 ) . We then use LitePT-S ( Yue et al., 2026 ) (pretrained on ScanNet ( Dai et al., 2017 ) ) to encode the point cloud. Finally, eight learned queries pool the scene encoder’s output into eight scene tokens through two attention blocks. We train only the input layer, the output projection, and the pooling blocks while the rest of the scene encoder remains frozen during training. In 20 % 20\% of training windows, we zero the image features.
blocks.zh: 每个场景点有12个12个频道来包装点的位置,表面正常,距离手和物体,高度高于支持平面,正常倾斜从垂直,曲率,和日志密度. 它还拥有32个PCA减量DINov3图像特性的32个频道(Siméoni等人,2025年)。 随后使用LitePT-S(Yue等人,2026年)(ScanNet(Dai等人,2017年)预训)编码点云. 最后,八个学到的问询将场景编码器的输出通过两个注意块汇集成八个场景符号. 我们只训练输入层,输出投影, 和集合块,而其余的场景编码器在训练期间仍然冷冻. 在20%的训练窗口中, 我们没有图像特性。

blocks.en: We also uniformly sample 10,000 10{,}000 points from the object mesh’s surface and use a frozen Uni3D-g encoder ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) to encode them. A trainable projection layer then maps the encoded vector to four object-shape tokens. We also add one context token for the object’s log scale and one for each hand’s MANO shape.
blocks.zh: 我们还统一抽取了10000 10{,} 000 点从对象的网状表面抽取出来,并使用冷冻的Uni3D-g编码器(周等人,2024年)来编码它们. 一个可训练的投影层然后将编码的矢量映射到四个对象形状的令牌. 我们还为对象的日志比例增加一个上下文符号,为每只手的MANO形状增加一个上下文符号。

In temporal infilling, the gap length and start are drawn uniformly, and the first and last frames are always observed. blocks.en: Trajectory losses. We supervise decoded wrist and object positions with squared error and decoded rotations of the wrists, object, and 15 15 finger joints of each hand with θ 2 / 2 \theta^{2}/2 , where θ \theta represents the angle to the reference rotation. These losses also include observed frames decoded by the Δ \Delta -codec based on predicted differences, in addition to masked frames.
blocks.zh: 轨迹损失. 我们监督手腕和物体的解码位置 手腕和物体的解码旋转 手腕和物体的解码旋转 手掌的15个15个手指关节 用\\ 2 / 2\theta\2}\/2,其中\theta代表了参考旋转的角度。 这些损失还包括根据预测差异由\\Delta -codec解码的观测到的帧,以及蒙面帧.

blocks.en: We also regularize smoothness and finger articulation. To improve smoothness, we penalize increases in the squared acceleration and jerk of the wrists and object over the reference within masked segments, with jerk weighted 1 / 30 1/30 relative to acceleration. For finger articulation, we penalize joint-limit violations and the MANO pose prior when they exceed the reference’s. Table 4 lists the joint limits.
blocks.zh: 我们还将光滑度和手指表达规范化。 为了提高光滑度,我们惩罚在蒙面区段内增加手腕和物体的平方加速度和比参照物多的混蛋,即相对于加速度的混蛋加权1/301/30。 在指头表达时,我们惩罚共同限制的违反行为,而且MANO在超过参考标准时会摆姿势。 表4列出了联合限额。

blocks.en: The fingertip-distance loss is the absolute error in fingertip-to-object distance, counted only for fingertips within 10 10 cm of the object in the reference. For each hand, we evaluate it on the last frame where the hand or the object is predicted and on up to 15 15 other such frames chosen at random. The attachment loss of Equation 3 applies to periods of at least two consecutive frames in which the hand touches the object in the reference. For each hand, we take up to 48 48 frames spread across these periods, longest first. Its velocity term also covers steps between observed and predicted frames within a contact period.
blocks.zh: 指尖-距离损失是指尖对对象距离的绝对错误,在参考文献中只计为指尖在物体10厘米以内. 对于每一只手,我们都会在手或物体预测的最后一个框架上加以评价,并且最多有15个其他这种框架是随机选定的。 附加方程式3的丢失适用于参考物中手触动对象的至少连续两个帧的期间. 每只手,我们用48个48帧 分布在这些时期,最短的第一。 其速度术语还涵盖接触期内观测到的与预测的帧之间的步骤。

Both summaries measure changes from the reference pose at the present frame, and when the hand or the object is predicted, they also include each wrist’s change relative to the object. We scale the dense summary so that its size does not depend on the number of predicted frames. Table 4 gives this scaling and how the landmark summary represents the final rotation change. We also penalize predicted objects that extend more than 10 10 mm below nearby supporting surfaces, such as tabletops.

blocks.en: Training. We train for 40,000 40{,}000 steps with AdamW ( Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019 ) and evaluate the final checkpoint (see Table 4 for the remaining settings). We sample windows with source and label-quality weights, up-weighting windows with a left hand by up to 10 × 10\times to balance supervision across hands. We also use a curriculum in which extracted videos make up about 23.5 % 23.5\% of sampled windows for the first 20,000 20{,}000 steps, then decrease linearly to 2 % 2\% by step 32,000 32{,}000 and stay there, to focus the end of training on the more accurate annotated data.
blocks.zh: 培训。 我们与AdamW(Loshchilov和Hutter, 2019年)一起训练40,000步, 我们用源头和标签质量的重量对窗户进行抽样,用左手对窗户进行提升,最多10×10×次,以平衡横跨双手的监督. 我们还使用一个课程,其中提取的视频在前20 000个20{}步骤中占采样窗口的23.5%、23.5%,然后通过第32 000个32{}步骤将线性下降至2%。

blocks.en: For augmentation, with probability 0.5 0.5 , we rotate the hands, object, and scene collectively around the vertical axis by a Gaussian angle with standard deviation 0.35 0.35 rad. Independently, with probability 0.5 0.5 , we also resample a 30 30 fps window at 30 30 , 15 15 , or 10 10 fps while maintaining the frame timestamps.
blocks.zh: 对于增强,用概率0.5 0.5,我们用一个高斯角度,用标准偏差0.35 0.35 rad,将手,物体和场景围绕垂直轴一起旋转. 独立地,用概率0.5 0.5,我们还在保持帧时间戳的同时,在30 30,15 15,或 10 10 英尺时重现一个30英尺的窗口.

blocks.en: Loss weights. Since our losses differ greatly in scale, we use gradient norms to set their weights instead of setting them manually. Before training, we set each loss weight so it contributes a target fraction of the flow-matching gradient by measuring its gradient norm on batches from the annotated datasets. Wrist and object position, the energy score, and the support penalty keep a weight of 1 1 , and the contact-classifier weight rises linearly from about zero to 0.1 0.1 over the first 5,000 5{,}000 steps. Table 5 lists the resulting weights.
blocks.zh: 减重. 由于我们的损失规模大不相同,我们使用梯度规范来设定它们的权重,而不是手工设定. 在训练之前,我们设定每个减重,以便通过从附加说明的数据集中分批测量其梯度标准,达到流量比比梯度的一个目标部分。 手腕和物体位置,能量分数,以及支持罚则保持1-1的重量,接触分类器的重量在前5000 5{,}000步中线性从大约0升至0.1. 表5列出了由此产生的权重。

blocks.en: Appendix B Extraction Pipeline Details
blocks.zh: 附录B 管道细节

blocks.en: B.1 Pipeline Implementation
blocks.zh: B.1 管道实施

blocks.en: We describe the exported trajectories, processing steps, and quality checks for the video extraction pipeline introduced in Section 3.4 .
blocks.zh: 我们描述了第3.4节引入的视频提取管道的出口轨迹、加工步骤和质量检查。

blocks.en: Exported trajectories. Each exported trajectory contains frames sampled at approximately 10 10 Hz, with their original video timestamps. It includes MANO parameters ( Romero et al., 2017 ) for up to two hands, per-frame validity flags for each hand, and the rotation and translation of a reconstructed object mesh. The export also includes an estimated gravity direction when available.
blocks.zh: 出口轨迹. 每个出口的轨迹都含有在大约10赫兹取样的帧,并带有其最初的视频时间戳。 它包括最多两只手的MANO参数(Romero等人,2017年),每只手的每帧有效性旗,以及一个重建对象网的旋转和翻译. 出口还包括估计的重力方向。

blocks.en: Clip selection and validation. We take candidate clips from Action100M’s timestamped action captions ( Chen et al., 2026a ) . Molmo 2 ( Clark et al., 2026 ) names the manipulated object from each caption, with no predefined object list, and clips where it names none are discarded. The same model is used again, this time on the video, to determine whether a hand is interacting with any objects. In clips that pass, it checks one frame per second to find when the interaction occurs, and these times decide which frames we use to locate the object. Clips are split at detected shot boundaries, and each shot of at least 4 4 seconds is processed independently.
blocks.zh: 剪辑选择与验证. 我们从Action100M的有时间标记的动作字幕(Chen等人,2026a)中, Mollmo 2 (Clark et al., 2026)从每个标题中命名被操纵的对象,没有预先定义的对象列表,并在其中命名无被丢弃的片段. 同样的模型再次被使用,这一次在视频中,以确定一只手是否与任何物体相互作用. 在通过时的片段中,它检查每秒一个帧以发现交互发生的时间,这些时间决定我们用来定位对象的帧. 剪切在检测到的射击边界上进行分割,每个至少4 4秒的镜头都是独立处理的.

blocks.en: Hand and object estimation. WiLoR ( Potamias et al., 2025 ) gives MANO hand estimates in each frame. We discard low-confidence detections and short-lived tracks, and reject the clip if no hand track remains. To find the object, we ask Molmo 2 ( Clark et al., 2026 ) to point to it in a frame using the name given in the clip’s caption. We remove outlier points and require the remaining points to lie near a hand whenever one is tracked in that frame. If we can’t find the object with enough points in up to four frames, we discard the candidate clip. SAM 3 ( Carion et al., 2025 ) then tracks the object mask forward and backward through the clip, starting from the accepted points.
blocks.zh: 手和物体估计。 WiLOR(Potamias等人,2025年)给出了每个帧的MANO手势估计. 我们放弃低信心的探测和短寿命的轨迹,如果手轨没有留下,就拒绝剪辑。 为了找到对象,我们请Molmo 2 (Clark et al., 2026)用剪辑标题中给出的名字在框中指向它. 我们删除最突出的点,要求其余点在跟踪到时靠近一个手。 如果我们找不到足够分数的物体, SAM 3(Carion et al.,2025)然后通过剪辑前后跟踪物体面具,从接受的点开始.

blocks.en: SAM 3D ( Chen et al., 2025 ) then reconstructs the object mesh from one frame, chosen to have a large object mask. Masks much larger than the adjacent frames or multi-part or oddly shaped are given lower priority. At other sampled frames, SAM 3D reuses this mesh to estimate the object’s pose and scale. We run the full reconstruction only when this fails for a frame.
blocks.zh: SAM 3D(Chen et al., 2025)然后从一个框架重建对象网,选择有一个大对象面具. 遮罩比相邻框架或多部分或奇特形状的遮罩要大得多,其优先级较低。 在其他采样帧中,SAM 3D重用这个网格来估计物体的姿势和规模. 我们只进行完全的重建 当这个失败的帧。

blocks.en: Object motion estimation. CoTracker3 ( Karaev et al., 2025 ) tracks points in the object mask, and depth from MoGe ( Wang et al., 2025a ) lifts them into 3D. RANSAC PnP ( Fischler and Bolles, 1981 ; Lepetit et al., 2009 ) gives initial object poses, which we refine before removing tracks with high reprojection error. Bundle adjustment then refines the poses and the points’ positions within the object together, with fixed camera poses. The Huber loss ( Huber, 1964 ) assesses agreement with image tracks, while additional penalties promote smooth rotations and maintain the estimated 3D shape. Rotations come from this fit and object centers from SAM 3D’s estimates. If no fit is found or if the median per-frame reprojection error is > 12 >12 pixels, we fall back on the rotation estimates from SAM 3D.
blocks.zh: 物体运动估计. CoTracker3(Karaev等人,2025年)在物体掩体中追踪点,从MoGe(Wang等人,2025年a)的深度将其提升为3D. RANSAC PnP(Fischler and Bolles,1981;Lepetit等人,2009年)给出了初始对象姿势,我们在移除有高重投影误差的轨道之前对其进行了细化. Bundle 调整后将姿势和点数在物体内的位置一起细化,并加上固定的相机姿势. Huber损失(Huber,1964年)评估与图像轨道的协议,而附加处罚则促进平滑旋转并维持估计的3D形状. 从SAM 3D的估算中, 如果找不到适合性,或者如果每帧重投射误差的中位数 > 12 > 12像素,我们就会从SAM 3D中回落到旋转估计值.

blocks.en: Joint optimization. We then fix the hand shape and size and jointly refine the hand and object poses. Although the object shape is fixed, we refine the object size estimated from MoGe depth with a single scale factor per clip. The objective penalizes interpenetration, fits the reprojected object to its mask, and maintains hand contact with the object. Other terms discourage abrupt motion, unnatural finger poses, and large deviations from the initial estimates. We also penalize changes in the hand’s position relative to the object and, during grasps, changes in its relative rotation.
blocks.zh: 联合优化. 然后我们修正手的形状和大小,并共同改进手和物体的姿势。 虽然物体形状是固定的,但我们用每个剪辑的单个尺度系数来精炼从MoGe深度估计的对象大小. 目标惩罚穿透,将重投影对象与面具相匹配,并与对象保持手接触. 其他术语阻止突然运动、非自然的手指和与初步估计的巨大偏差。 我们还惩罚改变手部相对于物体的地位,以及在掌握物体时改变相对旋转。

blocks.en: We optimize with Adam and a cosine learning-rate schedule in stages. In the initial frames, we align the wrists and fix those poses. We then refine the wrist and object motions, followed by the finger poses, and finally all of them together. A final stage again refines the wrists and fingers in frames with low tracking confidence and poor hand-object alignment by fixing the object and pulling each finger toward its position relative to the palm in nearby reliable frames. After optimization, we correct object rotation during occlusions, remove a learned depth bias, and smooth the remaining hand jitter (Appendix B.2 ).
blocks.zh: 我们优化了亚当 和余弦学习率时间表 分阶段。 在初始框中,我们调整手腕并固定这些姿势. 然后我们细化手腕和物体的动作, 然后是手指的姿势, 最后是所有它们一起。 最后一个阶段再次将手腕和手指精炼成框,跟踪信心低,手对准度差,方法是固定物体,将每个手指拉到附近可靠的框中相对掌上的位置. 在优化后,我们修正了在隔离期间的物体旋转,去除所学的深度偏差,并平滑剩余的手触(附录B.2 ).

blocks.en: Object scale and depth correction. An object’s reconstruction can change size and depth across frames and still match the image mask, since a larger object farther away casts the same silhouette. We correct this when the 95th-percentile object size is at least 1.35 1.35 times the 5th-percentile size. Each frame’s mesh is first rescaled to the clip’s median object size. Comparing its projected area with the observed mask area then gives a smooth depth correction, leaving out frames where hands cover at least half the projected object. We reject a correction with too few reliable observations or increased depth variation. Any hand in contact with the object shifts along with it, so the contact is maintained.
blocks.zh: 对象尺度与深度校正. 一个对象的重建可以改变大小和跨框架的深度,并且仍然与图像遮罩相匹配,因为一个更大的物体在更远处投出相同的斜线。 当95百分位物体大小至少是5百分位的1.35倍时,我们纠正了这一点. 每个帧的网格首先被调整到剪辑的中间对象大小。 然后将其预测区域与观测到的遮罩区域相比较,可以平滑地进行深度修正,将手至少覆盖一半预计物体的帧留出。 我们拒绝接受可靠观察太少或深度差异增加的更正。 任何与物体接触的手随它一起移动,所以联系保持.

blocks.en: Interaction intervals. We call a frame an interaction frame when the object is visible and a tracked hand is within 5 5 cm of its surface. Consecutive interaction frames form intervals, and we merge intervals separated by at most 2 2 seconds. We then extend each interval by up to 0.75 0.75 seconds on both sides to include the frames where the hand approaches the object or releases it. Frames where the estimated object pose jumps abruptly are likely reconstruction errors. We leave them out, and no interval is merged or extended across them. We export each interval as a trajectory if it lasts at least 2.5 2.5 seconds and includes at least eight frames. Trajectories from the same clip do not overlap.
blocks.zh: 交互间隔. 当物体可见,跟踪手在其表面5厘米以内时,我们称一个帧为相互作用框架. 连续的相互作用框架形成间隔,我们最多用2 2 秒将间隔合并. 然后,我们将两侧的间隔延长0.75 0.75秒,以包括手靠近物体或释放物体的帧。 估计对象突然跳跃的框架可能是重建错误 。 我们不让他们进去,没有时间间隔被合并或延长。 如果每个间隔至少持续2.5秒并包括至少8个帧,则我们导出为轨迹。 同一片段的轨迹并不重叠.

blocks.en: Final pose refinement. We adjust each trajectory’s object position so that the projected silhouette more closely resembles the observed mask. Each modification is restricted to 0.30 0.30 m of translation and 35 ∘ 35^{\circ} of rotation. We consider a hand to be grasping an object if it remains within 4 4 cm of it for multiple consecutive frames. To maintain their relative stance throughout a grip, we adjust each frame and move the hand with the object. Next, without altering finger articulation, we smooth the hand’s rotation in relation to the object during grasps. Lastly, we relocate each hand by up to 8 8 mm to minimize residual hand-object penetration.
blocks.zh: 最后摆姿势完善. 我们调整每个轨迹的物体位置,使投射的光圈更接近观测到的面具。 每次修改限制在翻译的0.30 0.30米和旋转的35 ∘ 35^{\circ}. 我们认为,如果一个物体在连续的多个帧内保持在4-4厘米以内,那么它就是在抓住它。 为了保持他们的相对姿势,我们调整每个框架,用物体移动手. 接下来,在不改变手指表达方式的情况下,我们将手相对于物体的旋转平滑。 最后,我们把每只手移到最多8 8毫米处,以尽量减少残余的手物体穿透。

blocks.en: Gravity estimation. We estimate gravity from a supporting surface, such as a table or the floor, in the MoGe depth maps of several trajectory frames. The surface must appear consistently across these frames and lie below the hands, the object, and most of the scene. We favor large surfaces near the interaction, especially one the object rests on. A wall can meet these conditions too, since the hands and the object are in front of it. But for a wall to be the floor, the camera would usually have to be rolled far to the side or pointed sharply upward. People rarely film their hands like that, so we reject these surfaces. There are two more cases that we skip, because in both of them we cannot tell which way is up. A surface the camera sees at a grazing angle could face up or down. A surface facing the camera squarely could be a wall in front of the camera or a table filmed from straight above. Gravity is the normal of the selected surface, pointing away from the interaction; if no surface qualifies, we leave it undetermined.
blocks.zh: 引力估计. 我们在数个轨迹框架的MOGe深度图中,从表或底部等辅助表面估算引力。 表面必须始终如一地出现在这些框架上,并位于手,物体和大部分场景下方. 我们更喜欢靠近相互作用的大型表面, 特别是物体所依赖的一个。 墙也可以满足这些条件,因为手和物体在墙前. 但为了让墙成为地板,相机通常必须向侧面向远滚动或尖锐向上. 人们很少拍到这样的手, 所以我们拒绝这些表面。 我们还有两件案子要跳过,因为在这两件案子中,我们无法分辨是哪条路走的。 摄像头在放牧角度看到的表面可以向上或向下看。 镜头正对面的表面可能是镜头前面的墙,或者从正上方拍摄的桌子. 重力是所选表面的正常现象,指向相互作用;如果没有表面合格,我们就让它不确定.

blocks.en: Quality filtering. We keep only trajectories that agree with the video. The projected object must match the outline and size of its tracked mask, and we reject trajectories in which the object changes shape or size or moves abruptly. A hand must also stay within 5 5 cm of the object in at least 25 % 25\% of the frames. Further checks catch shot boundaries, excessive hand-object penetration, and object masks that follow the hand rather than the object. We also drop trajectories where the hand touches the object in 3D but, in the image, almost never touches its mask. Lastly, we ask Molmo 2 to point to “the object held in the hand” in several frames, and we reject the trajectory if it often returns no point or points far from our tracked mask (i.e., we are likely tracking the wrong object).
blocks.zh: 质量过滤. 我们只保留与视频一致的轨迹. 投影对象必须与其履带面具的轮廓和大小相符,我们拒绝物体改变形状或大小或突然移动的轨迹. 一只手还必须在至少25%的25\%帧中停留在物体的5 5cm以内. 进一步检查捕捉到射出的界限,过度的手物体穿透,以及随手而不是随物体的物体口罩. 我们还将手在3D中触摸物体的轨迹放下,但在图像中几乎从未触碰过它的面具. 最后,我们请Molmo 2在几个框中指出“手持的物体”,如果轨迹常常离我们的履带面具不返回任何点或点(即我们很可能跟踪错误的物体),我们就拒绝。

blocks.en: B.2 Refinement Details
blocks.zh: B.2 改进细节

blocks.en: Object rotation. When the object is occluded for at least three consecutive frames, the grasping hand’s motion guides its rotation only when contact is stable and the camera rotates slowly. During the occlusion, the object rotates more closely with the hand, with the correction growing gradually as the occlusion begins and shrinking as it ends. We reject corrections that introduce large rotation jumps.
blocks.zh: 物体旋转. 当物体至少连续三个帧被占据时,抓取手的动作只在接触稳定,相机旋转缓慢时才能引导其旋转. 在封存期间,物体与手旋转比较紧密,随着封存的开始,修正逐渐增加,随着结束而缩小. 我们拒绝引入大规模旋转跳跃的更正。

blocks.en: Bias denoiser. A separate denoiser learns to recover clean trajectories from simulated extraction errors. It trains on 11,568 11{,}568 windows of 50 50 frames from DexYCB and HOT3D, sampled at 10 10 Hz, excluding the 129 129 segments from the sequences we use to evaluate refinement. The simulated errors are designed to reproduce the observed errors in the extraction pipeline. For instance, hands and objects are positioned too near or too far from the camera, their positions are disturbed over several frames, and the object’s orientation changes gradually.
blocks.zh: 比亚斯·德诺瓦 一个单独的denoiser学习从模拟提取错误中恢复干净的轨迹. 它在11,568 11{,}568个窗口上运行,50帧的窗口来自DexYCB和HOT3D,在10 10 Hz取样,不包括我们用来评价完善的序列中的129 129个段. 模拟错误旨在复制提取管道中观察到的错误。 例如,手和物体的位置离相机太近或太远,它们的位置在几个框架上被扰动,物体的方向逐渐改变。

blocks.en: The denoiser receives the hand and object poses at each frame, including finger articulation, and predicts corrections that we add to the standardized input states. It is an eight-layer bidirectional transformer with width 384 384 , six attention heads, and feedforward width 1024 1024 . We train it for 15,000 15{,}000 steps with batch size 256 256 , learning rate 2 × 10 − 4 2\times 10^{-4} , and 500 500 warmup steps. The loss is squared reconstruction error with weights of 10 10 for translation, 3 3 for rotation, and 1 1 for finger articulation, plus a velocity term with weight 0.5 0.5 that encourages the recovered motion to match the clean trajectory.
blocks.zh: denoiser接收每个帧的手和物体的姿势,包括手指的表达,并预测我们添加到标准化输入状态的校正. 它是一个八层双向变压器,宽度384 384,6个注意头,向导宽度1024 1024. 我们训练15,000 15{,}000步 批量大小256 256, 学习率2×10 − 4 2\times 10^{-4}和500500步热身。 损失为方形重建误差,翻译重为10 10,旋转重为3 3,手指发音重为1 1,加上重量0.5 0.5的速度术语,鼓励恢复的运动与干净的轨迹相匹配.

blocks.en: Applying the correction. On extracted trajectories, we use only part of this output: how far each hand and the object should move toward or away from the camera. We average these corrections over the trajectory and apply the same shift at each frame. To maintain their relative positions, the object and any hands in contact combine their shifts and move together. Next, we smooth each wrist’s position and rotation over three consecutive sampled frames. We do the same for the finger rotations, which we also keep within anatomical limits.
blocks.zh: 应用更正. 在提取的轨迹上,我们只使用这一输出的一部分:每一只手和物体应该向相机方向移动或远离相机的距离. 我们平均在轨迹上进行这些修正,并在每个框架上采用同样的转变。 为了保持相对位置,物体和任何接触的手将它们的班次结合在一起,一起移动. 接下来,我们将每个手腕的位置平滑,并在三个连续的取样框上旋转。 手指旋转也是这样, 解剖范围也是这样。

blocks.en: Evaluation. Table 6 evaluates refinement on 30 30 DexYCB and 28 28 HOT3D sequences. Full refinement follows the procedure described above, which keeps only the denoiser’s constant depth shift. We compare the final recipe with the raw, unrefined poses and two other refinement variants: one that applies every denoiser correction and one that takes a five-frame moving average of the raw poses. Full refinement lowers the median wrist error from 106.4 106.4 to 88.6 88.6 mm on DexYCB and from 191.2 191.2 to 158.7 158.7 mm on HOT3D. Although applying every denoiser correction reduces depth bias about as much as full refinement, it increases hand surface error on both datasets and object rotation drift on HOT3D. Moving-average smoothing slightly lowers the error on DexYCB but raises it on HOT3D.
blocks.zh: 评价。 表6评估了30个DexYCB和28个HOT3D序列的完善情况。 完全完善遵循了上述程序,该程序仅保持了Denoiser的不断深度转移。 我们把最后的配方与原始的,未经精炼的姿势和另外两个精炼变体进行比较:一个是采用每个凹凸的修饰,另一个是采用五个框架移动的原始姿势平均值。 全面完善后,手腕中位误差从DexYCB的106.4106.4降至88.688.6毫米,HOT3D上的191.2191.2降至158.7158.7毫米. 虽然应用每一个denoiser校正会减少深度偏差,大约可以达到完全的精度,但它会增加HOT3D上两个数据集的手表误差和物体旋转漂移. 移动平均平滑略降低DexYCB上的错误,但在HOT3D上提高.

blocks.en: We evaluate the extraction pipeline of Section 3.4 on the EPIC-Contact test set ( Bansal et al., 2026 ) with the authors’ released evaluator and fitted reference poses (Table 7 ). Unlike HOPformer, our pipeline is not trained on EPIC-Contact. It produces trajectories for 215 215 of the 237 237 test clips, and we score both methods on these clips. Since our trajectories are sampled at about 10 10 Hz, we sample HOPformer’s predictions at the same frames for metrics that depend on frame rate. Our hand joint error is lower than HOPformer’s ( 16.0 16.0 vs. 19.7 19.7 mm), and so is our motion deviation ( 10.6 10.6 vs. 13.8 13.8 mm). Our contact deviation ( 34.6 34.6 vs. 20.8 20.8 mm) and hand-object relative position error ( 71.8 71.8 vs. 64.7 64.7 mm) are higher, reflecting the main limitation of the extracted trajectories, namely absolute depth and hand placement relative to the object.

The 256 256 annotated windows come from 168 168 recordings: 36 36 from DexYCB; 35 35 each from HO3D, HOT3D, OakInk2, SHOW3D, and TACO; 24 24 from HO-Cap; and 21 21 from H2O. blocks.en: How extraction error affects internet-video scores. We evaluate predictions on internet videos against our own extracted trajectories, so extraction errors can affect the results. Much of what Appendix B.2 reports, however, is a constant offset per clip, mostly in depth ( 45 45 – 62 % 62\% of the squared position error on DexYCB, 77 % 77\% on HOT3D). An offset like this largely cancels. If a clip sits 10 10 cm too far from the camera, the observed frames the model receives sit 10 10 cm too far as well, and so does the reference. What remains drifts slowly over the clip, is also mostly in depth, and this part does affect the scores. On clips that pass our quality checks, a true motion of 50 50 – 150 150 mm comes out 10 10 – 15 % 15\% too short, and the error in that motion is smaller across the image than in depth, with medians of 28 28 versus 49 49 mm for objects and 41 41 versus 55 55 mm for wrists.

blocks.en: Physical metrics. Finger error (Table 9 ) is the angle between predicted and reference rotations, averaged over the 15 15 finger joints of each hand. For closed object meshes, we measure how deeply hand vertices penetrate the object and the percentage of vertices inside it. Joint limits follow Table 4 and are strict, since 14.8 % 14.8\% of joint poses in the annotated references exceed them. A violation therefore counts only when the predicted joint exceeds a limit and the reference joint does not, and we report violations as a percentage of all evaluated joint poses.
blocks.zh: 物理度量衡. 手指误差(表9)是预测和参考旋转之间的角度,平均在每只手的15个手指关节上. 对于密闭的物体膜,我们测量手顶部的深层穿透物体及其内侧的顶部百分比. 联合限制与表4相同,而且很严格,因为附加说明的参考资料中14.8%的连带限制超过了这些限制。 因此,只有当预计联合体超过限额且参照联合体没有时,违反情况才算数,我们报告违反情况占所有评估联合体的百分比。

blocks.en: Interaction metrics. The hand-object metrics of Table 10 use frames where the hand and object are both present and at least one of them is generated. A fingertip touches the object when it is within 10 10 mm of its surface. Tip error is the fingertip position error relative to the object on frames where the reference hand touches the object, and contact F1 accepts predicted contact up to two frames earlier or later than the reference. A reference grasp is a run of at least three frames in which at least two reference fingertips touch the object. On each grasp frame, the movement error is the difference between how the predicted and reference fingertips have moved relative to the object since the grasp began, averaged over the five fingertips. The frame is held when at least two predicted fingertips touch the object and this error is at most 10 10 mm, slipping when a predicted fingertip touches the object but the frame is not held, and detached when every predicted fingertip is at least 20 20 mm away. Other frames are unclassified, and we report the percentage of grasp frames in each class.
blocks.zh: 互动度量衡。 表10的手对象度量衡是使用框,其中手和物体都存在,并且至少产生其中之一. 指尖在物体表面10 10 毫米范围内触碰物体. 提示错误(Tip error)是相对于参考手触碰对象的帧上对象的指尖位置错误,联系人F1接受预测的接触,最多比引用早或晚两个帧. 参考抓取是至少三个帧的运行,其中至少有两个参考指尖触及对象. 在每个抓取框上,运动误差是自抓取开始以来,预测的指尖和参考的指尖相对于对象移动的区别,平均在五个指尖上. 当至少两个预言的指尖触碰物体而这个误差最多为10 10 mm时,框会保持,当一个预言的指尖触碰物体但框没有被保持时,这个误差会滑动,当每个预言的指尖至少20 20 mm外时,会脱落. 其他的帧是未分类的,我们报告每个类别中抓取帧的百分比。

blocks.en: Each window’s interaction score averages the 20 20 samples, and the two hands when both are present. We then average windows within each task, separately for annotated data and internet videos, and unlike for the other metrics, every annotated window counts equally regardless of its dataset. Tasks count equally, and so do annotated data and internet videos. For differences between models, we estimate 95 % 95\% confidence intervals by resampling video segments 5,000 5{,}000 times, using the same resampled segments for both models.
blocks.zh: 每个窗口的相互作用平均得分是20个样本,而两个样本都在场时的两只手。 与其他衡量标准不同的是, 每个附加说明的窗口无论它的数据集如何, 任务数相等,附加说明的数据和互联网视频也一样。 对于模型之间的差异,我们估计95%的95QQ的置信间隔,方法是对视频片段进行5000 5{,}000次的复制,对两种模型都使用相同的复刻片段.

blocks.en: Learned baselines. For Table 2 , we use the USST ResNet-18, ObjectForesight EPIC-DiT, and Uni-Hand SAM-3D-Body/DINOv2 checkpoints, the variant of each that scores best on this benchmark. ObjectForesight takes one step per video frame, which scores better than one step per 1 / 55 1/55 s, the frame interval of its training videos. The ForeHand4D checkpoint was trained on DexYCB, HOT3D, and H2O, and the Uni-Hand checkpoints on robot demonstrations. Methods that use depth get monocular depth from Depth Anything 3 for MotionForesight and from MoGe-2 for the others, including our model. General Flow and MolmoMotion get action text for each clip, from dataset labels where available and a generic description otherwise. All predictions start from the reference at the last observed frame. To ensure a fair comparison with hand forecasting methods, we shift their predictions to start at the observed wrist, removing a constant placement offset that would otherwise dominate their error. For methods that predict 3D point trajectories, we fit a rotation and translation per frame without changing object size, and we interpolate all predictions to the reference timestamps.

blocks.en: Losses and relation tokens. Two parts of the model are there for hand-object contact, the physical losses and the relation tokens (Section 3.2 ). The physical losses are the attachment, fingertip-distance, joint-limit, MANO pose prior, and support penalty terms, which supervise contact and plausibility on decoded trajectories (Section 3.3 ). We train one ablation without them and one without the relation tokens. The latter still has the attachment and fingertip-distance losses, so its contact is supervised. Removing either part weakens the grasp. In the main model, fingertip error during contact is 7 7 – 9 % 9\% lower, contact F1 is 68.2 % 68.2\% (versus 65.3 % 65.3\% and 66.3 % 66.3\% ), and 24.9 % 24.9\% of grasp frames are detached (versus 29.1 % 29.1\% and 28.1 % 28.1\% ; Table 10 ). The closer grasp costs a little. Slipping, i.e., frames where the hand touches the object without following the reference grasp, rises to 47.5 % 47.5\% (from 44.5 % 44.5\% and 45.5 % 45.5\% ), and the share of penetrating vertices to 4.20 % 4.20\% (from 3.94 % 3.94\% ), at about the same depth. The main model’s hand ADE and FDE are also 2 2 – 8 % 8\% lower in every column of Table 9 .

blocks.en: Scene conditioning. Nearby surfaces and obstacles limit where an object can go, and the scene encoder tells the model about them. We also train without it, i.e., without scene geometry or DINOv3 features (the object shape is still given). The hands are barely affected, within 2 % 2\% on ADE and FDE, and detach about as often ( 26.0 % 26.0\% versus 24.9 % 24.9\% of grasp frames). The objects are not. We rotate the hands, object, and scene together around the vertical axis and resample windows at lower frame rates (Appendix A ) so that the model does not depend on the usual orientation and frame rate of each training dataset. Without this augmentation, every ADE and FDE in Table 9 gets worse. The main model’s are 3 3 – 9 % 9\% lower, and the gap is largest for best-of- 20 20 hand FDE. The ablation’s hand also detaches from the object more often ( 27.8 % 27.8\% versus 24.9 % 24.9\% of grasp frames). blocks.en: Interpreting the interaction scores. Each sample is scored against a single reference, frame by frame, so a sample that follows a plausible but different hand path is penalized. The scores therefore depend on how much of the hand’s path the model has to generate. Fingertip error during contact is 26 26 mm in temporal infilling and 46 46 mm when the hand motion is given, but 60 60 – 93 93 mm in the five tasks where the model generates most of the hand’s path. Table 10 averages all seven tasks. For scale, stay-put on the same frames has a fingertip error of 92 92 mm and a contact F1 of 55 % 55\% . The main model beats it on both in every task, and its overall fingertip error is 28 % 28\% lower.

blocks.en: Appendix F Limitations
blocks.zh: 附录F 限制

blocks.en: We extract the internet-video trajectories with pretrained models, and their mistakes end up in our training data. MoGe estimates depth from a single image, where a large object far away casts the same silhouette as a small one nearby, so the hands and object can sit at the wrong distance from the camera. Refinement fixes much of this, though not all, and extracted motions come out a bit short. WiLoR loses the fingers when the object covers them and occasionally takes a hand-shaped object for a hand. SAM 3D can flip an object’s orientation between frames, and we often fail to pose thin objects such as spoons or cables. On tripod shots, MegaSaM sometimes reports a small camera motion, which then shows up as motion of an object resting on the table. We also reject most candidate clips, many only after all these models and the per-clip optimization have run, so extracting more videos takes a lot of compute.
blocks.zh: 我们用预先训练过的模型提取互联网视频轨迹,他们的错误最终会出现在我们的训练数据中. MoGe从一个单一的图像中估计出深度,一个遥远的大型物体将附近的一个小物体投出相同的圆柱形,因此手和物体可以坐错距离相机. 完善解决了大部分问题,虽然不是全部问题,但提取出来的动议略短。 WiLOR在对象覆盖时会失去手指,偶尔也会为手取一个手形对象. SAM 3D可以在帧之间翻转对象的方向,我们经常不能摆出像勺子或电缆这样的细小对象. 在三脚架镜头中,MegaSAM有时会报告一个小型的相机运动,然后以一个物体在桌子上休息的动作出现. 我们也拒绝大多数候选剪辑,很多是在所有这些模型和每个剪辑的优化运行之后,所以提取更多的视频需要大量的计算.
